Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "please turn these notes into a plain internal status update about the april 29–may 12 payroll export, for finance, not a how-to. finance generated the csv from the payroll system on may 14 and saved it in the finance shared folder at 10:20 am. it has 86 employee rows, with 3 held because their cost center fields are blank; no other held rows were reported. the included-row gross pay total is $241,680, and that matches the payroll system total for those same 83 rows. bank details haven't been checked yet. say the export is for finance review and isn't a payment submission. mention that the missing cost centers need to be filled in before the held rows can be included, but don't imply anyone has supplied them. keep the numbers and dates, and don't call the file approved. make the last part a clear assessment: finance can review the 83 included rows now, while the 3 held rows can join only after their cost centers are filled in; payment readiness hasn't been assessed. don't add a conclusion about the whole payroll run, since only this export and these 86 rows are in scope. keep it readable, in a couple of short paragraphs, with a final section that states the assessment.", "output": "Write a plain internal status update for Finance about the April 29–May 12 payroll export. This should be an update, not a how-to, and should cover only this export and its 86 employee rows.

Include these details: Finance generated the CSV from the payroll system on May 14 and saved it in the Finance shared folder at 10:20 a.m. Three rows are held because their cost center fields are blank; no other held rows were reported. The included-row gross pay total is $241,680, matching the payroll system total for those same 83 rows. Bank details have not been checked. State that the export is for Finance review, not a payment submission. The missing cost centers must be filled in before the held rows can be included, but do not imply that anyone has supplied them. Do not call the file approved.

Use a couple of short, readable paragraphs and end with a clear assessment section: Finance can review the 83 included rows now, while the three held rows can join only after their cost centers are filled in. Payment readiness has not been assessed. Do not draw a conclusion about the whole payroll run."}]
